**Reject: the change removes the `fs.dir("out", Mode::ReadWrite)` narrowing, and the description does not call for that.**

**What was there before.** `export` took `fs: &Fs` but immediately narrowed it to `out` with `Mode::ReadWrite`. Every later step used only that narrowed value: making subdirectories, unlinking the old entry and writing the report. Those steps were confined to `out` by the capability itself, not just by how paths were built.

**What the change does.** It drops that line. Every step now goes through the full, unnarrowed `fs`:

- line 30: `fs.create_dir_all(path.parent())`
- line 36: `fs.remove_file(&part)`
- line 42: `fs.open_with(&part, …create_new)`
- line 44: `fs.rename(&part, &path)`
- line 45: `fs.remove_file(&part)` on failure

The only things keeping these inside `out` are the string prefix `Path::new("out").join(name)` and the name checks. Those checks reject `..`, `.`, empty components, leading `/` and backslashes. They do not stop symlinks. Any symlink already under `out` (for example `out/x -> /etc`) is now followed by the full-authority `Fs`. That lets `export` create directories, unlink files, create files and rename files anywhere the root `Fs` reaches. Before, the `out` capability bounded all of this.

**Why the description doesn't cover it.** The described behaviour (a temporary `<name>.part` beside the report under `out`, created with `create_new`, then renamed over the report) works just as well through the narrowed `out` directory capability. Nothing in the description needs file-system authority outside `out`. Keeping `out` and calling `out.open_with`, `out.rename` and `out.remove_file` would deliver the change without widening authority.

```json
{"verdict": "reject", "findings": [{"line": 30, "item": "export", "authority": "fs", "what": "Creates directories through the unnarrowed root Fs instead of the out-only ReadWrite capability, so a symlink under out can redirect directory creation anywhere the root Fs reaches."}, {"line": 36, "item": "export", "authority": "fs", "what": "Unlinks files through the unnarrowed root Fs, so via a symlinked directory under out it can delete files outside out."}, {"line": 42, "item": "export", "authority": "fs", "what": "Creates and writes the temporary file through the unnarrowed root Fs rather than the out-only capability, allowing writes outside out via symlinks."}, {"line": 44, "item": "export", "authority": "fs", "what": "Renames files through the unnarrowed root Fs, so it can replace files outside out when a path component under out is a symlink."}, {"line": 45, "item": "export", "authority": "fs", "what": "Removes the temporary on failure through the unnarrowed root Fs, again not confined to out as the dropped fs.dir narrowing ensured."}]}
```
